newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia firm to build power plant in Sabah town.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia firm to build power plant in Sabah town.

text.p: Malaysian firm Stratavest Sdn Bhd plans to build a 240 million ringgit power station in the Borneo-island town of Sandakan to help overcome power disruptions, the national Bernama news agency said on Monday.

Expected to start commercial operation in 1998, the Libaran power station would have an installed power production capacity of 60 megawatts, it said. Sandakan is located on the east coast of Malaysia's Sabah state.

The company was granted a 21-year concession to generate and sell electricity under an agreement signed with the Sabah Electricity Board (SEB) in January, Stratavest executive chairman Abdul Rahim Mohamad told reporters after the signing of several agreements related to the project.
Abdul Rahim said the build, operate and own power station will use low speed diesel engines provided by Mitsui Engineering and Shipbuilding Co Ltd.
Power produced by the power station will be sold at 16.10 Malaysian cents per unit to SEB.

Abdul Rahim said some 20 percent of the project's financing would be from internally-generated funds and 80 percent from local borrowing. Stratavest officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
